clue.text: Strike back and cut the talk!

indicators.note: back tells us the word for strike is read from right to left

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
to lance is to cut open with a blade

explanation.surface: An angry exclamation: hit back and stop all this chatter!
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives PAR from the word for strike; the exclamation mark is only surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking or its idiom, so it can stand for talk.

clue.text: A paling protester

definitions.meaning: a pointed stake used in a fence
a striker standing outside a workplace to deter others

explanation.surface: A pale, feeble demonstrator.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed fence stake is one sense; a striker barring the gates is the other.

clue.text: To live in was a confrere's idea

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Moving in with someone was a colleague's suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across confRERE'S IDEa; 'was a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there.

clue.text: Respect for a Moslem leader in dreadful situation

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for dreadful

parts.note: dire describes a dreadful situation, as in dire straits

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Moslem

explanation.surface: Esteem for an Islamic ruler who is in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moslem leader' looks like EMIR, but it is just its first letter, M, which goes into DIRE after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard or esteem.

clue.text: Place where new car buyer keeps a little book

indicators.note: keeps means the shuffled letters hold the book inside them
new suggests the letters of the words car buyer are made into something fresh

parts.note: NT, short for New Testament, is a book in abbreviated form

explanation.surface: Somewhere a new car's owner keeps a pocket book.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR BUYER is rearranged and holds NT after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury is a cathedral city in Kent, England.

clue.text: Belief in the cashless society?

parts.note: one sense is simply belief or trust; the other is the buy-now-pay-later system that a society without cash would run on

explanation.surface: Wondering about faith in a world where nobody carries money.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means trust in someone's word, and also the deferred-payment arrangements that replace coins and notes.

clue.text: No one seaman turns on a number if wise

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first part sits above the next
turns means the run of words before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
a tar is a sailor
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Not one sailor keeps turning on a crowd, if he knows what's good for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses NOITAR to give RATION, which then sits on A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means sensible and guided by reason.

clue.text: Joint veto resolution taken in parliament

indicators.note: taken in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the parliament

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: resolution means the letters of veto are worked out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A combined veto motion is passed by the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' gives OVET and 'taken in' sets it within the parliament: the Dail is the lower house of Ireland's legislature, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking joint in woodwork.

clue.text: Dwelling with English people in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: in places the English people inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
men means people

explanation.surface: Housing English people in makeshift shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' wraps the shelter round the English people; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, so a dwelling.

clue.text: Order came sent replacement window

indicators.note: to order things is to put them into a new sequence, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ordered a new window and it has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' reads as part of the surface; CAMESENT rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window that opens like a door.

clue.text: He's a good man, on the level

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
on the level, i.e. level or flat, gives even

explanation.surface: Praising a man as virtuous and honest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'He's': a man's name stands for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven is a boy's given name, so it names a particular he.

clue.text: A little cod is in consequence approved of

indicators.note: in here means the fish is placed inside the word for consequence

parts.note: an end is a result or outcome, a consequence
a dorse is a young cod, a little one

explanation.surface: Approving of something because a small fish turned up as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' needs the old fishmonger's word for a young cod, rarely met outside crosswords; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give backing or sanction, so endorsed means sanctioned or backed.

clue.text: Base and asinine artisan

definitions.meaning: the lowest part or foundation of something
the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream who is given a donkey's head

explanation.surface: A low, stupid working man.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside of anything is its foot or lowest point, and Shakespeare's weaver who turns ass-headed bears that same name.

clue.text: Look over agricultural machinery for a man prepared to do business

definitions.text: a man prepared to do business

parts.note: to con is to study or look over carefully
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Inspecting farm equipment for a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor undertakes to supply goods or do work for an agreed fee.

clue.text: Doing away with a bar, go in to make alternative arrangement

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of letters is a rearrangement of the words before it

explanation.surface: Abolishing a pub's bar, someone goes in to sort out different plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of A BAR GO IN TO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrogation is the formal repeal or abolition of a law, so it is a doing away with.

clue.text: Long to hold up brief thank-you letter

indicators.note: to hold means the longing word contains the other piece

parts.note: to aspire is to long for something

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the short word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ta is a short informal thank you

explanation.surface: Wanting to delay a short note of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives AT in a down clue, and 'to hold' puts it within the word for long. The letter meant is the breathed sound h.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the sound h, or a letter representing a breathed sound.

clue.text: Plants as once it might have been

indicators.note: might have been suggests these letters could once have been in another order

explanation.surface: Wondering what these flowers might once have been.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconites are poisonous plants of the buttercup family, including monkshood and winter aconite.

clue.text: A case for the fashionable with some position

parts.note: in means fashionable
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: An argument for the trendy, holding some sort of view.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example or occurrence, a case in point.

clue.text: Scold after minute bit isn't very good

indicators.note: after places the word for scold behind the other piece

parts.note: a second is a small bit of a minute
to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: Being told off after a tiny slip-up is not much fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the scolding word second. 'Rate' meaning scold is an old usage; the definition is a phrase describing poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre or inferior is not of the first quality.

clue.text: Trained revolutionary carrying a listening device

indicators.note: carrying means the revolutionary holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a red is a communist, a revolutionary
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A drilled insurgent wearing a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' suggests a bug, but it is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Reared means brought up or raised, as a child trained in its manners.

clue.text: To have dinner about six is perfect

indicators.note: about means the dining word goes round the number

parts.note: to dine is to have dinner
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: Dining at around six o'clock is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the dining word round the Roman numeral; 'is' only links. Divine as 'perfect' is a gushing informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used informally for delightful or excellent, as in a divine meal.

clue.text: Pledge causing a dilemma

definitions.meaning: an old sense: to promise solemnly

explanation.surface: A promise that lands someone in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an old verb for promising, as of marriage vows; the other is a predicament.

clue.text: Fed by the hotel, as is natural

indicators.note: by puts the word for fed next to the hotel

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
ate means fed or took food

explanation.surface: A guest fed by the hotel, which is only natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, part of one's nature from birth.

clue.text: Stuff of vital interest

definitions.meaning: cloth or fabric, or matter in general
important or relevant, as evidence pertinent to a case

explanation.surface: Something important is described as stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric or substance is one sense; the other is the legal sense of evidence that is significant to the issue.

clue.text: Wait for a series of races to terminate

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race series on the Isle of Man
to end is to terminate

explanation.surface: Waiting for a run of race meetings to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy, a famous series of motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend on someone is to wait on or serve them.

clue.text: Rousing carol with bitter content

indicators.note: content here means contents: the bitter word is what the carol holds inside it

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
tart means sharp or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: A stirring Christmas carol with gloomy lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' is read as a noun, the contents: the bitter word is what the carol holds. 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting from sleep is being roused with a jolt, so rousing and starting are both waking up suddenly.

clue.text: A quarter bloom in Spring

parts.note: E for east, one of the four quarters of the compass
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A small patch of flowers coming out in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the festival falls in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian festival of the Resurrection is held each year in spring.

clue.text: An inclination for treading in a mess

indicators.note: something in a mess is jumbled up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who likes stamping about in muck.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, and an inclination is also a slope or incline.
